coordinates.note: Campus-level coordinate from Wikipedia's infobox, shown as approximate. The Ricochet detector's own paper gives only its distance from the reactor core (8.8 m), not an absolute coordinate, so the exact detector hall position is not sourced. The signs are consistent with the location: Grenoble, France is in the northern hemisphere (positive latitude) and east of the prime meridian (positive longitude).

name: ILL Grenoble reactor hall
notes: The Ricochet detector sits 8.8 m from the ILL reactor core (arXiv:2208.01760); no separate, more precise detector-hall coordinate was found in a fetched source, so this campus-level point is used for the site record.

summary.plain: The research-reactor building at the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, France, where the Ricochet experiment sits about 9 metres from the reactor core to catch its antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Reactor hall of the ILL 58.3 MW research reactor, Grenoble, France; hosts the Ricochet CEvNS detector array 8.8 m from the reactor core.
